documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
documents.author: Dr. Anita Patel
documents.text: Admission Date: 02/14/2026. Discharge Date: 02/19/2026. Chief Complaint: worsening shortness of breath and 6 lb weight gain over one week. History: 78-year-old woman with chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF 30%), permanent atrial fibrillation on warfarin, hypertension, and stage 3 chronic kidney disease. She presented with dyspnea at rest, orthopnea, and bilateral lower-extremity edema. Examination: JVP elevated at 14 cm, bibasilar crackles, 2+ pitting edema. Labs: BNP 1450 pg/mL, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (baseline 1.6), potassium 6.8 mmol/L, INR 6.2. Chest radiograph showed pulmonary vascular congestion and small bilateral pleural effusions. Echocardiogram: EF 30%, moderate mitral regurgitation. Hospital course: treated with IV furosemide with net negative 4.2 L, potassium lowered with sodium polystyrene sulfonate and insulin/dextrose, warfarin held for supratherapeutic INR. Diagnoses: acute decompensated heart failure, hyperkalemia, coagulopathy due to warfarin, CKD stage 3. Disposition: home with cardiology follow-up in 7 days. Discharge medications: furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg BID, sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg BID, spironolactone held. Follow-up labs in 3 days.

documents.title: Echocardiogram - Transthoracic
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: Transthoracic echocardiogram. Left ventricle is moderately dilated with severe global hypokinesis. Ejection fraction estimated at 30%. Moderate mitral regurgitation. Left atrium moderately dilated. Right ventricular systolic pressure estimated at 48 mmHg. Small pericardial effusion. No intracardiac thrombus. Impression: HFrEF with EF 30%, moderate MR, pulmonary hypertension.

documents.title: Progress Note - Cardiology
documents.author: Dr. Anita Patel
documents.text: Subjective: dyspnea improved, now comfortable at rest. Objective: BP 104/62, HR 78 irregular, SpO2 96% on room air, weight down 2.8 kg. Exam: crackles at bases, JVP 9 cm, trace edema. Labs: potassium 5.4, creatinine 2.1, INR 2.8. Assessment: improving decompensated heart failure; hyperkalemia resolving; INR therapeutic after warfarin hold. Plan: continue IV diuresis, transition to oral furosemide, repeat BMP in the morning, resume warfarin at reduced dose.

documents.title: Primary Care - Diabetes and CKD Follow-up
documents.author: Dr. Lena Brooks
documents.text: Chief Complaint: diabetes follow-up. 63-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus for 14 years, stage 3b chronic kidney disease, hypertension, and obesity. Reports polyuria and fatigue; denies chest pain. Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, empagliflozin 10 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg. Exam: BP 148/86, BMI 34, 1+ bilateral edema. Labs: HbA1c 9.4%, glucose 312 mg/dL, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min/1.73m2, potassium 5.4 mmol/L, urine albumin-creatinine ratio 480 mg/g. Assessment: uncontrolled type 2 diabetes, CKD stage 3b with albuminuria, hyperkalemia, hypertension not at goal. Plan: add semaglutide, reduce metformin to 500 mg BID, stop lisinopril temporarily, low-potassium diet, repeat BMP in 2 weeks, diabetes education referral.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note - Asthma Exacerbation
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: Emergency Department Note. Chief Complaint: wheezing and shortness of breath for two days after a viral upper respiratory infection. 35-year-old woman with moderate persistent asthma. She used albuterol every two hours overnight without relief. Exam: RR 26, SpO2 93% on room air, diffuse expiratory wheezes, speaking in short sentences. Peak flow 280 L/min (baseline 480). Chest radiograph: hyperinflation without focal consolidation or pneumothorax. Treatment: albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers x3, oral prednisone 60 mg, magnesium sulfate 2 g IV. Reassessed after treatment: SpO2 97%, peak flow 420 L/min, wheezing decreased. Assessment: moderate asthma exacerbation triggered by viral URI. Plan: prednisone 50 mg daily x5 days, continue inhaled corticosteroid-formoterol, asthma action plan reviewed, return precautions.

documents.title: Chest Radiograph - PA and Lateral
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: Chest radiograph PA and lateral. Lungs are hyperinflated with flattened diaphragms. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal. Impression: hyperinflation consistent with obstructive airway disease; no acute infiltrate.

documents.title: Admission History and Physical
documents.author: Dr. Hannah Lee
documents.text: Chief Complaint: fever, productive cough, and confusion for two days. 50-year-old man with hypertension and former tobacco use. Temperature 39.1 C, BP 92/58, HR 118, RR 28, SpO2 89% on room air. Examination: ill-appearing, crackles and egophony at the right base. Labs: WBC 22.4, lactate 4.2 mmol/L, procalcitonin 8.1 ng/mL, creatinine 1.6, sodium 132. Chest CT: dense right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms and a small parapneumonic effusion. Blood cultures drawn. Assessment: sepsis secondary to community-acquired pneumonia, likely Streptococcus pneumoniae. Plan: ceftriaxone and azithromycin, 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus, supplemental oxygen, ICU consultation, repeat lactate.

documents.title: CT Chest with Contrast
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: CT chest with intravenous contrast. Dense consolidation in the right lower lobe with air bronchograms. Small right parapneumonic pleural effusion. No pulmonary embolism. No pneumothorax. Mediastinal lymphadenopathy reactive in appearance. Impression: right lower lobe pneumonia with small parapneumonic effusion.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation - Headache
documents.author: Dr. Ravi Shah
documents.text: Chief Complaint: recurrent throbbing headaches for six months. 37-year-old woman with a history of episodic migraine without aura. Headaches occur 3-4 times per month, unilateral left temporal, associated with photophobia, nausea, and occasional visual shimmering lasting 20 minutes. No fever, neck stiffness, weakness, or speech difficulty. Neurological examination normal, including fundoscopy and cranial nerves. MRI brain without contrast: no acute infarct, mass, or hemorrhage; a few nonspecific white matter foci. Assessment: migraine without aura, stable; medication overuse headache not present. Plan: continue sumatriptan as needed, start propranolol 20 mg BID for prevention, headache diary, follow up in 8 weeks.

documents.title: MRI Brain without Contrast
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: MRI brain without and with diffusion-weighted imaging. No acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, mass lesion, or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci are age-appropriate. A few tiny nonspecific subcortical white matter hyperintensities. Orbits and paranasal sinuses unremarkable. Impression: no acute intracranial abnormality.

documents.title: Oncology Consultation - Rising PSA
documents.author: Dr. Priya Desai
documents.text: Oncology Consultation. Chief Complaint: rising PSA and bone pain. 89-year-old man with a history of localized prostate adenocarcinoma diagnosed in 2019, treated with external beam radiation. Current PSA 18.4 ng/mL, up from 4.2 six months ago. Reports new dull lower back pain. Examination: ECOG 1, no focal neurologic deficit, back tender to palpation at L3. Bone scan: increased uptake in the L3 vertebral body and right posterior iliac crest, concerning for osseous metastases. Labs: hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, creatinine 1.2, alkaline phosphatase 168 U/L, PSA 18.4. Assessment: biochemically recurrent prostate cancer with suspected bone metastases. Plan: CT abdomen/pelvis, MRI lumbar spine, start androgen deprivation therapy with leuprolide, bone health optimization with denosumab, palliative care referral, follow-up in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Whole-Body Bone Scan
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: Whole-body bone scan. Focal increased radiotracer uptake in the L3 vertebral body and right posterior iliac crest. No other suspicious foci. Kidneys and bladder visualize normally. Impression: two foci suspicious for osseous metastatic disease; correlate with MRI.

documents.title: Primary Care - Hypothyroidism Follow-up
documents.author: Dr. Lena Brooks
documents.text: Chief Complaint: fatigue and cold intolerance. 30-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis on levothyroxine 50 mcg daily. Reports fatigue, constipation, and dry skin for three months. Examination: bradycardia 58 bpm, dry skin, delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes, no goiter. Labs: TSH 8.9 mIU/L, free T4 0.7 ng/dL, hemoglobin 11.9, vitamin D 22 ng/mL. Assessment: inadequately treated primary hypothyroidism, vitamin D insufficiency. Plan: increase levothyroxine to 75 mcg daily, recheck TSH in 6 weeks, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily, counsel on adherence.

documents.title: Hepatology Consultation - Decompensated Cirrhosis
documents.author: Dr. Miriam Goldstein
documents.text: Hepatology Consultation. Chief Complaint: abdominal distension and fatigue. 56-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and prior variceal bleed. Reports increasing abdominal girth over three weeks and early satiety. Examination: scleral icterus, spider angiomata, tense ascites, no hepatic encephalopathy. Labs: platelets 78, total bilirubin 3.4 mg/dL, INR 1.9, albumin 2.6 g/dL, creatinine 1.1, sodium 129, AST 68, ALT 42. CT abdomen: nodular cirrhotic liver, moderate ascites, splenomegaly, patent portal vein, no hepatocellular carcinoma. Assessment: decompensated cirrhosis with ascites and coagulopathy; hyponatremia. Plan: therapeutic paracentesis with albumin, spironolactone 100 mg and furosemide 40 mg daily, sodium restriction, band surveillance in 2 weeks, transplant evaluation referral, alcohol cessation counseling.

documents.title: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with Contrast
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Cirrhotic liver with nodular contour and moderate ascites. Spleen enlarged at 15 cm. Portal and splenic veins patent. No focal hepatic lesion. Small hiatal hernia. Impression: cirrhosis with portal hypertension and moderate ascites; no hepatocellular carcinoma.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note - COPD Exacerbation
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: Emergency Department Note. Chief Complaint: increased sputum and breathlessness. 72-year-old woman with severe COPD (FEV1 38% predicted), former smoker, and hypertension. Reports three days of purulent sputum and worsening dyspnea. Examination: RR 24, SpO2 88% on room air, barrel chest, diffuse wheezes and coarse crackles. Chest radiograph: hyperinflation and increased bibasilar markings, no consolidation or pneumothorax. Labs: WBC 12.8, hemoglobin 14.2, sodium 136, potassium 4.1, bicarbonate 32. Treatment: controlled oxygen to SpO2 90-92%, ipratropium-albuterol nebulizers, prednisone 40 mg, doxycycline, noninvasive ventilation considered but not required. Assessment: COPD exacerbation, likely bacterial bronchitis. Plan: prednisone taper, antibiotic course, inhaler technique review, pulmonary rehab referral.

documents.title: Chest Radiograph - COPD Exacerbation
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: Chest radiograph. Hyperinflated lungs with flattened hemidiaphragms. Increased bibasilar bronchovascular markings. No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax. Impression: changes of COPD without acute infiltrate.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note - Renal Colic
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: Emergency Department Note. Chief Complaint: severe right flank pain radiating to the groin for six hours, associated with nausea and hematuria. 44-year-old man with no prior kidney stones. Temperature 37.2 C, BP 138/84, HR 96. Examination: right costovertebral angle tenderness, no peritoneal signs. Urinalysis: 3+ blood, 1+ protein, negative nitrite and leukocyte esterase. CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: 6 mm obstructing stone at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydronephrosis. Labs: creatinine 1.0, WBC 12.1, sodium 139. Assessment: right ureteral stone with mild obstruction; no signs of infection. Plan: ketorolac, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, strain urine, urology follow-up, return for fever or uncontrolled pain.

documents.title: CT Abdomen and Pelvis without Contrast
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast. A 6 mm calcified stone is seen at the right ureterovesical junction with mild proximal right hydronephrosis. No left-sided stone. No appendicitis or diverticulitis. Impression: obstructing right distal ureteral calculus with mild hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note - Abdominal Pain
documents.author: Dr. Hannah Lee
documents.text: Emergency Department Note. Chief Complaint: periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant for 18 hours, with nausea and low-grade fever. 24-year-old woman, no significant past medical history. Temperature 38.0 C, HR 102, BP 118/72. Examination: tenderness at McBurney point with guarding and rebound. Labs: WBC 15.2, hemoglobin 12.8, sodium 137. Ultrasound abdomen: enlarged non-compressible appendix measuring 9 mm with surrounding fat stranding and a small amount of free fluid; no appendicolith. Assessment: acute uncomplicated appendicitis. Plan: NPO, IV fluids, ceftriaxone and metronidazole, general surgery consultation for laparoscopic appendectomy.

documents.title: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: Ultrasound abdomen and pelvis. The appendix is enlarged, non-compressible, and measures 9 mm in diameter with surrounding hyperechoic fat stranding. A small amount of free fluid is present in the right lower quadrant. No abscess. Impression: sonographic findings compatible with acute appendicitis.

documents.title: Stroke Neurology Note - Code Stroke
documents.author: Dr. Ravi Shah
documents.text: Stroke Neurology Note. Chief Complaint: sudden right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking. 82-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and atrial fibrillation not on anticoagulation. Last known well 07:30; arrived 08:05. NIHSS 9 for right facial droop, right arm and leg weakness, and mild expressive aphasia. CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage; early ischemic changes not visualized. CT angiography: occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery M2 segment. Labs: glucose 118, INR 1.1, platelets 210, creatinine 1.3. Given alteplase at 08:40 after blood pressure control. Admitted to the stroke unit. MRI brain confirmed acute left MCA territory infarct. Assessment: acute ischemic stroke, left MCA M2 occlusion, atrial fibrillation. Plan: stroke unit monitoring, dysphagia screening, start anticoagulation after 24 hours, physical and speech therapy, echocardiogram.

documents.title: MRI Brain with Diffusion-Weighted Imaging
documents.author: Dr. M. Rosen
documents.text: MRI brain with diffusion-weighted imaging. Restricted diffusion in the left insular cortex and left frontal operculum consistent with acute infarction in the left middle cerebral artery territory. No hemorrhage. No mass effect. MRA demonstrates occlusion of the left M2 segment. Impression: acute left MCA territory infarct.

Reports adherence to medications with no acute distress. Examination: BP 148/88, HR 82, afebrile, cardiopulmonary examination unremarkable. Assessment: healthy adult with borderline LDL cholesterol. Plan: diet and exercise counseling, repeat lipids in 6 months, age-appropriate screening.

documents.title: Primary Care - Upper respiratory infection
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: Upper respiratory infection visit. Chief Complaint: sore throat and nasal congestion for four days. 69-year-old man with a history of upper respiratory infection. Reports adherence to medications with no acute distress. Examination: BP 153/77, HR 83, afebrile, cardiopulmonary examination unremarkable. Assessment: viral upper respiratory infection. Plan: supportive care, fluids, rest, return if fever or shortness of breath develops.

documents.title: Primary Care - Mechanical low back pain
documents.author: Dr. Lena Brooks
documents.text: Mechanical low back pain visit. Chief Complaint: lower back pain after lifting. 62-year-old woman with a history of mechanical low back pain. Reports adherence to medications with no acute distress. Examination: BP 130/80, HR 84, afebrile, cardiopulmonary examination unremarkable. Assessment: mechanical low back pain without red flags. Plan: NSAIDs as needed, physical therapy referral, return precautions for weakness or incontinence.

documents.title: Primary Care - Hyperlipidemia follow-up
documents.author: Dr. Lena Brooks
documents.text: Hyperlipidemia follow-up visit. Chief Complaint: cholesterol follow-up. 55-year-old man with a history of hyperlipidemia follow-up. Reports adherence to medications with no acute distress. Examination: BP 135/83, HR 85, afebrile, cardiopulmonary examination unremarkable. Assessment: hyperlipidemia not at LDL goal. Plan: increase atorvastatin to 40 mg nightly, repeat lipid panel in 8 weeks, continue Mediterranean diet.

documents.title: Primary Care - Gastroesophageal reflux disease
documents.author: Dr. Samuel Ortiz
documents.text: Gastroesophageal reflux disease visit. Chief Complaint: heartburn and regurgitation. 49-year-old woman with a history of gastroesophageal reflux disease. Reports adherence to medications with no acute distress. Examination: BP 140/86, HR 68, afebrile, cardiopulmonary examination unremarkable. Assessment: gastroesophageal reflux disease without alarm features. Plan: omeprazole 20 mg daily before breakfast, avoid late meals, weight management, reassess in 6 weeks.
